impact_assessment.why: The user asked to continue idea-catcher and then implement it on AIKit like Aegean Reforge
impact_assessment.benefits: Completes the uncommitted registry features and makes AIKit ship the complete idea-catcher tool source, with bidirectional sync to projects/idea-catcher

[1/1] Move brand disclosure into its own section, add license tags everywhere, raise test ceilings to 20/500 ms

impact_assessment.why: The user rejected the inline disclosure, asked for license tags on every existing and future project, and approved 20 ms/500 ms test ceilings.
impact_assessment.benefits: A dedicated Brand Assets section, license metadata on all projects and new projects, and realistic test budgets under host load.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: README section and new/publish topic lists change; dependency: none; concurrency: sequential project metadata updates; state: license_topics added to project memory.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Live topic verification for all projects, pinned license/section tests, ADR-244/245, and full Phase 4 gates.

[1/4] Remove the standalone Reforge repository layer, fix the repair/delivery defects it exposed, refresh knowledge and gates

impact_assessment.why: The user wants Reforge integrated into AIKit only; the duplicate projects/aegean-reforge checkout and one-way sync file create two sources of truth and already drifted.
impact_assessment.benefits: One canonical source for Reforge, no bidirectional sync conflicts, less documentation ambiguity, and a safer repair commit scope.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: reforge repo subcommands and reforge-sync.json disappear; dependency: none beyond stdlib; concurrency: docs/tests edited while another AIKit session may touch shared files; state: no persisted schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Remove the layer atomically, keep reforge.py plus reforge/ as the entrypoints, update every reference and test, and re-read shared files immediately before staging.

checkpoints.description: Task 'reforge-aikit-integration' completed successfully.
[1/5] Integrate Idea Catcher into AIKit only: move its private register to the AIKit root, drop the repo sync layer, archive and remove projects/idea-catcher

impact_assessment.why: The user wants the Idea Catcher tool integrated into AIKit, its found ideas kept but invisible to the public, the local standalone repo archived, and projects/idea-catcher removed
impact_assessment.benefits: One canonical Idea Catcher source, no bidirectional sync drift, private register data preserved outside public commits, and a smaller CLI surface
impact_assessment.risks: contract: repo subcommands, idea-catcher-sync.json and the projects register layout disappear; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: shared docs/tests may be touched by another session; state: register data moves to an ignored root folder, no public schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Move data atomically, ignore it before staging, update every reference and test, archive the full repository first, then run all Phase 4 gates and verify git status carries no idea data

checkpoints.description: [5/5] Idea Catcher integrated into AIKit only; private register moved to git-ignored .idea-catcher/; repo sync layer removed; standalone repo archived to Desktop and projects/idea-catcher deleted; 595 unit + 66 integration tests and every gate pass; checklists: passed
Task 'idea-catcher-integration' completed successfully.
[1/4] Make Reforge review every changed file and record its run in AIKit's real task ledger

impact_assessment.why: Running Reforge on AIKit skipped 20 of 20 changed files as 'Python only' and reported 'no AIKit task ledger', so it could not review the agent's own step-by-step changes
impact_assessment.benefits: Every changed text file is inspected with structural checks, coverage is honest about binary files only, and an in-progress audit is visible to a cold start in .agents/task_ledger.json
impact_assessment.risks: contract: audit_window/api payload gains a reviewed count, skipped now means binary only; dependency: stdlib only (tomllib optional); concurrency: reforge state and ledger locks unchanged; state: stage entry gains an additive reviewed count
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep Python AST rules byte-identical, add text rules as a separate module, test both layouts, refresh knowledge and ADR, and run every gate

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Reforge reviews every changed text file (JSON/TOML parse, Markdown fences, conflict markers) and finds the ledger by name; project memory keyed on .aikit/project.json; 600 unit + 66 integration tests and every gate pass; ADR-253; checklists: passed
Task 'reforge-review-changes' completed successfully.
[1/5] Make Reforge AI-driven and concurrency-safe: per-project isolation, AI review of stage changes, validated AI fixes

impact_assessment.why: The user wants Reforge usable on several projects at once and wants it to analyse changes with AI before applying fixes, not only run static detectors
impact_assessment.benefits: Independent projects audit concurrently with isolated locks and state; a stage is reviewed by a read-only AI agent with a bounded diff; validated AI suggestions become applied, tested, reviewable repairs
impact_assessment.risks: contract: audit/run gain AI flags and payload/state fields, findings gain source/patch fields; dependency: optional opencode CLI and free model, no new Python deps; concurrency: several opencode subprocesses and per-project locks; state: additive schema keys only
impact_assessment.mitigation: Resolve roots before locking, keep AI optional and gracefully skipped, validate every AI path/line/patch against the stage, run tests and gates with rollback, and pin each behaviour with tests and ADR-254

checkpoints.description: [5/5] Reforge reviews each stage with a read-only AI agent on a free model and applies only validated patches; per-project resolved locks keep parallel audits isolated; 604 unit + 69 integration tests and every gate pass; ADR-254; checklists: passed
